subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 6-year-old boy with a profound T-cell immunodeficiency is found to have a defect in de novo purine synthesis. Cultured lymphoblasts from the patient incorporate radiolabeled precursors into IMP at less than 10% of the normal rate, and the metabolic team is mapping which atoms of the purine ring come from which precursor.
question: Which of the following amino acids is incorporated as a whole molecule, providing both carbon and nitrogen atoms to the purine ring?
explanation_correct: Glycine is incorporated intact into the developing purine ring, contributing carbon atoms 4 and 5 as well as nitrogen 7. The remaining atoms come from glutamine (nitrogens 3 and 9), aspartate (nitrogen 1), N10-formyl tetrahydrofolate (carbons 2 and 8), and carbon dioxide (carbon 6). This is why de novo purine synthesis requires glycine, glutamine, aspartate, and tetrahydrofolate.

explanation_incorrect.A: Aspartate donates only its amino group (nitrogen 1) to the purine ring; its carbon skeleton is not incorporated.
explanation_incorrect.B: Glutamine donates amide nitrogens (nitrogens 3 and 9) but not carbon atoms to the ring.
explanation_incorrect.C: Serine is a one-carbon donor through tetrahydrofolate metabolism but is not incorporated into the purine ring.
explanation_incorrect.E: Alanine is not a purine precursor; it serves mainly as a carrier of nitrogen and carbon from muscle to liver in the glucose-alanine cycle.

educationalObjective: Glycine is the only amino acid incorporated intact into the purine ring, contributing carbons 4 and 5 and nitrogen 7.
